paragraphs: Unless this Form 10-K indicates otherwise or the context otherwise requires, the terms "we," "our," "us," "Sysco," or the "company" as used in this Form 10-K refer to Sysco Corporation together with its consolidated subsidiaries and divisions.

Sysco Corporation is the global leader in selling, marketing and distributing food and related products to customers who prepare meals away from home. This includes restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments, entertainment venues, and more.

Founded in 1969, Sysco commenced operations as a public company in March 1970 when the stockholders of nine companies exchanged their stock for Sysco common stock. Since our formation, we have grown from $115 million to our all-time high of $84.6 billion in annual sales in fiscal 2026, both through internal expansion of existing operations and acquisitions.

Sysco's fiscal year ends on the Saturday nearest to June 30th. This resulted in a 52-week year ended June 27, 2026 for fiscal 2026, a 52-week year ended June 28, 2025 for fiscal 2025 and a 52-week year ended June 29, 2024 for fiscal 2024. We will have a 53-week year ending July 3, 2027 for fiscal 2027.

Sysco Corporation is organized under the laws of Delaware. The address and telephone number of our executive offices are 1390 Enclave Parkway, Houston, Texas 77077-2099, (281) 584-1390. This annual report on Form 10-K, as well as all other annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and amendments to reports filed or furnished by Sysco pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (Exchange Act), with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) are available free of charge on Sysco's website at www.sysco.com as soon as reasonably practicable after they are electronically filed with or furnished with the SEC. Sysco also periodically provides certain information for investors on its website at www.sysco.com. This includes press releases and other information about financial performance, information on environmental, social and governance matters, and details related to Sysco's annual meeting of stockholders. The information contained on the websites referenced in this Form 10-K is not incorporated by reference into this filing.

On March 30, 2026, Sysco Corporation entered into an agreement and plan of merger (the Merger Agreement) pursuant to which Sysco Corporation will acquire JRD Unico, Inc. and Warehouse Realty LLC (collectively, Jetro Restaurant Depot or JRD) through a series of transactions (the merger and the other transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, the Transactions). JRD is a leading U.S. wholesale cash-and-carry foodservice provider serving smaller, independent restaurants and businesses. JRD operates 167 large-format warehouse stores across 35 states that serve more than 725,000 independent restaurants and foodservice operators with a broad assortment of fresh and low-priced products.

Sysco has agreed to pay approximately $29.1 billion to JRD equity holders, comprised of $21.6 billion in cash, subject to customary adjustments, and 91.5 million shares of Sysco Holdings common stock. Following the closing of the Transactions, former holders of Sysco Corporation common stock and former equity holders of JRD will own shares of Sysco Holdings Corporation, which are expected to be listed for trading on the NYSE. JRD's equity holders are expected to hold approximately 16% and our stockholders are expected to hold approximately 84% of the outstanding Sysco Holdings common stock in the aggregate. Refer to Note 12, "Debt and Other Financing Arrangements" for discussion on how Sysco is financing the acquisition of JRD and Note 10, "Derivative Financial Instruments" for details on how Sysco is hedging the interest rate risk associated with its financing arrangements.

This Transactions are expected to close by the third quarter of Sysco's fiscal 2027, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including regulatory clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act.

Sysco distributes food and related products to restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments and other foodservice customers. Our primary operations are in North America and Europe. Under the accounting provisions related to disclosures about segments of an enterprise, we have combined certain operations into three reportable segments. "Other" financial information is attributable to our other operations that do not meet the quantitative disclosure thresholds.

•U.S. Foodservice Operations – primarily includes (a) our U.S. Broadline operations, which distribute a full line of food products, including custom-cut meat, seafood, produce, specialty Italian, specialty imports and a wide variety of non-food products and (b) our U.S. Specialty operations, which include our FreshPoint fresh produce distribution business, our Buckhead | Newport Meat & Seafood specialty protein operations, our growing Italian Specialty platform anchored by Greco & Sons, Inc., our Edward Don restaurant equipment and supplies distribution business, our Asian specialty distribution company and a number of other small specialty businesses that are not material to the operations of Sysco;

•International Foodservice Operations – includes operations outside of the United States (U.S.), which distribute a full line of food products and a wide variety of non-food products. The Americas primarily consists of operations in Canada, Bahamas, Costa Rica and Panama, as well as our export operations that distribute to international customers. Our European operations primarily consist of operations in the United Kingdom (U.K.), France, Ireland and Sweden;
•SYGMA – our U.S. customized distribution operations serving quick-service chain restaurant customer locations; and
•Other – primarily our hotel supply operations, Guest Worldwide.

Foodservice operating sites distribute a full line of food products and a wide variety of non-food products to both independent and chain restaurant customers, hospitals, schools, hotels, industrial caterers and other venues where foodservice products are served. SYGMA operating sites distribute a full line of food products and a wide variety of non-food products to certain chain restaurant customer locations. Selected financial data for each of our reportable segments, as well as financial information concerning geographic areas, can be found in Note 21, "Business Segment Information," in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8.

headings: Risk Factor Summary
Industry and General Economic Risks
Business and Operational Risks
Risks Related to the Transactions

Our industry is characterized by low margins, and periods of significant or prolonged inflation or deflation affect our product costs and may negatively impact our profitability and results of operations.
A shortage of qualified labor and increases in labor costs could adversely affect our business and materially reduce earnings.
Global health developments and economic uncertainty resulting from global public health crises may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Unfavorable macroeconomic conditions, as well as unfavorable conditions in particular local markets, may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
Economic and political instability and changes in laws and regulations could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
Competition and the impact of GPOs may reduce our margins and make it difficult for us to maintain our market share, growth rate and profitability.
Adverse publicity about us or lack of confidence in our products could negatively impact our reputation and reduce earnings.
Our relationships with long-term customers may be materially diminished or terminated, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our anticipated change to the mix of locally managed customers versus multi-unit customers could reduce our gross and operating margins.
Changes in consumer eating habits could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Expanding into new markets and complementary lines of business presents unique challenges and may not be successful, and failure to successfully expand may adversely affect the implementation of our business strategy.
Changes in applicable tax laws or regulations and the resolution of tax disputes could negatively affect our financial results.

If our products are alleged to have caused injury, illness, or death, or to have failed to comply with governmental regulations, we may need to recall or withdraw our products and may experience product liability claims.
We may incur significant costs to comply with environmental laws and regulations, and we may be subject to substantial fines, penalties or third-party claims for non-compliance.
If we are unable to finance and integrate acquired businesses effectively, our earnings per share could be materially adversely affected.

We rely on technology in our business, and any cybersecurity incident, other technology disruption or delay in implementing new technology could negatively affect our business and our relationships with customers.
paragraphs: The following discussion of "risk factors" identifies the most significant factors that may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial position and future financial performance. This information should be read in conjunction with Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations and the consolidated financial statements and related notes contained in this report. The following discussion of risks is not all inclusive but is designed to highlight what we believe are the most significant factors to consider when evaluating our business. These factors could cause our future results to differ from our expectations expressed in the forward-looking statements identified within "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and from other historical trends.

The following is a summary of the principal risks that could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows, or the value of our securities. This summary does not describe all of the risks we face and should be read together with the more detailed discussion of the risk factors set forth below in this Item 1A and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us, or that we currently deem immaterial, may also impair our business.

•Our industry is characterized by low margins, and periods of significant or prolonged inflation or deflation affect our product costs and may negatively impact our profitability and results of operations.
•A shortage of qualified labor and increases in labor costs could adversely affect our business and materially reduce earnings.
•Global health developments and economic uncertainty resulting from global public health crises may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
•Unfavorable macroeconomic conditions, as well as unfavorable conditions in particular local markets, may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of Sysco's financial condition, results of operations and liquidity and capital resources for the fiscal years ended June 27, 2026 and June 28, 2025 should be read as a supplement to our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying notes contained in Item 8 of this report, and in conjunction with the "Forward-looking Statements" section set forth in Part II and the "Risk Factors" section set forth in Item 1A of Part I. All discussion of changes in our results of operations from fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2024 has been omitted from this Form 10-K, but may be found in Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" of our Form 10-K for the year ended June 28, 2025, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on August 22, 2025.

Sysco distributes food and related products to restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments and other foodservice customers. Our primary operations are in North America and Europe. Under the accounting provisions related to disclosures about segments of an enterprise, we have combined certain operations into three reportable segments. "Other" financial information is attributable to our other operations that do not meet the quantitative disclosure thresholds.

•U.S. Foodservice Operations – primarily includes (a) our U.S. Broadline operations, which distribute a full line of food products, including custom-cut meat, seafood, produce, specialty Italian, specialty imports and a wide variety of non-food products and (b) our U.S. Specialty operations, which include our FreshPoint fresh produce

distribution business, our Buckhead | Newport Meat & Seafood specialty protein operations, our growing Italian Specialty platform anchored by Greco & Sons, Inc., our Edward Don restaurant equipment and supplies distribution business, our Asian specialty distribution company and a number of other small specialty businesses that are not material to the operations of Sysco;

•International Foodservice Operations – includes operations outside of the United States (U.S.), which distribute a full line of food products and a wide variety of non-food products. The Americas primarily consists of operations in Canada, Bahamas, Costa Rica and Panama, as well as our export operations that distribute to international customers. Our European operations primarily consist of operations in the United Kingdom (U.K.), France, Ireland and Sweden;
•SYGMA – our U.S. customized distribution operations serving quick-service chain restaurant customer locations; and
•Other – primarily our hotel supply operations, Guest Worldwide.

We estimate that we serve about 18% of an approximately $377 billion annual foodservice market in the U.S. based on industry data obtained from Technomic, Inc. (Technomic) as of the end of calendar year 2025. Technomic projects the market size to increase to approximately $390 billion by the end of calendar year 2026. From time to time, Technomic may revise the methodology used to calculate the size of the foodservice market and, as a result, our percentage can change not only from our sales results, but also from such revisions. We also serve certain international geographies that vary in size and amount of market share.

According to industry sources, the foodservice, or food-away-from-home, market represents approximately 56% of the total dollars spent on food purchases made at the consumer level in the U.S. as of the end of calendar year 2025.

Our fiscal 2026 results reflected sales growth of 3.9% as compared to fiscal 2025, driven by inflation and volume growth, including contributions from recent acquisitions. Sales increased across our U.S. Foodservice Operations, International Foodservice Operations, and SYGMA segments. Gross profit increased 4.5% as compared to fiscal 2025, primarily due to our strategic sourcing efforts and higher volumes from local customers. Operating income increased 0.2% as compared to fiscal 2025, primarily due to gross profit gains, partially offset by increased sales headcount investments, increased restructuring and transformational project costs, higher incentive compensation, and higher acquisition and due diligence costs. We consider restructuring and transformational project costs and acquisition and due diligence costs to be "Certain Item" expenses (as defined below). Excluding Certain Item expenses, adjusted operating income increased 2.6% as compared to fiscal 2025. See below for a comparison of our fiscal 2026 results to our fiscal 2025 results, both including and excluding Certain Items (as defined below).
Below is a comparison of results from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2025:
•Sales: ◦increased 3.9%, or $3.2 billion, to $84.6 billion;
•Operating income: ◦increased 0.2%, or $7 million, to $3.1 billion; ◦adjusted operating income increased 2.6%, or $91 million, to $3.6 billion;
•Net earnings: ◦decreased 3.9%, or $71 million, to $1.8 billion; ◦adjusted net earnings increased 1.4%, or $31 million, to $2.2 billion;

paragraphs: 除非本 Form 10-K 有特別說明或語境另有要求，否則本 Form 10-K 中使用的 "we," "our," "us," "Sysco," 或 "company" 皆指 Sysco Corporation 連同其合併子公司與分公司。
Sysco Corporation 是全球在銷售、行銷與分發食品及相關產品至外食餐飲客戶的領導者。這包括餐廳、醫療與教育機構、旅館、娛樂場所等。
Sysco 於 1969 年成立，並於 1970 年 3 月以公開公司形式開始營運，當時九家公司的股東將其股票換為 Sysco 普通股。自我們成立以來，我們從 1.15 億美元成長至 2026 年財務年度的歷史高點 846 億美元的年銷售額，這包括現有業務的內部擴張與收購。
Sysco 的財務年度結算日為 6 月 30 日最近的星期六。這導致 2026 年財務年度為 52 週年度，結算日為 2026 年 6 月 27 日；2025 年財務年度為 52 週年度，結算日為 2025 年 6 月 28 日；2024 年財務年度為 52 週年度，結算日為 2024 年 6 月 29 日。我們預計 2027 年財務年度為 53 週年度，結算日為 2027 年 7 月 3 日。

Sysco Corporation 根據特拉華州法律設立。我們總部的地址與電話號碼為德州休士頓 1390 Enclave Parkway, Houston, Texas 77077-2099, (281) 584-1390。本 Form 10-K 年度報告，以及所有其他年度 Form 10-K 報告、季度 Form 10-Q 報告、現況 Form 8-K 報告，以及根據 1934 年證券交易所法案第 13(a) 或 15(d) 章節提交或提供給證券交易委員會（SEC）的報告修正案，皆可在 Sysco 網站 www.sysco.com 上免費取得，自這些報告電子提交或提供給 SEC 後即時取得。Sysco 也會定期在其網站 www.sysco.com 上提供投資者資訊。這包括新聞稿及其他財務表現資訊、環境、社會與治理相關資訊，以及 Sysco 股東年會相關細節。本 Form 10-K 中提及的網站資訊並未納入本檔之參考。

Sysco Corporation 於 2026 年 3 月 30 日與 JRD Unico, Inc. 及 Warehouse Realty LLC（合稱 Jetro Restaurant Depot 或 JRD）簽訂合併協議（合併協議），根據該協議，Sysco Corporation 將透過一系列交易取得 JRD（合併及合併協議中預期的其他交易，稱為 Transactions）。JRD 是美國領先的現金與現購食品服務供應商，服務小型獨立餐廳與企業。JRD 在 35 個州運營 167 家大型倉庫商店，服務超過 725,000 家獨立餐廳與食品服務經營者，提供廣泛的新鮮且價格低廉的產品。

Sysco 同意向 JRD 股東支付約 291 億美元，包含 216 億美元現金（根據慣例調整）及 9150 萬股 Sysco Holdings 普通股。交易完成後，Sysco Corporation 股東與 JRD 原股東將持有 Sysco Holdings Corporation 股票，預期將在紐約證券交易所上市交易。JRD 股東預期將持有約 16% 的 Sysco Holdings 普通股，而 Sysco 股東預期將持有約 84% 的 Sysco Holdings 普通股。有關 Sysco 資助收購 JRD 的資訊，請參閱附註 12，"債務及其他融資安排"；有關 Sysco 貸款安排的利率風險對沖資訊，請參閱附註 10，"衍生金融工具"。
這些交易預計在 Sysco 2027 財務年度的第三季完成，前提是符合慣例的交易條件，包括根據哈特-斯科特-羅德諾法案的監管批准。
Sysco 供應食品及相關產品至餐廳、醫療與教育機構、住宿設施及其他餐飲客戶。我們的主要營運地區為北美與歐洲。根據會計準則中關於企業分部揭露的規定，我們將某些營運單位合併為三個應報告分部。"其他"財務資訊則歸屬於不達成量化揭露門檻的其他營運單位。

•美國餐飲營運 – 主要包括 (a) 我們的美國廣線營運，提供完整的食品產品線，包括客製化切割肉類、海鮮、蔬果、義大利特色產品、進口特色產品以及廣泛的非食品產品，以及 (b) 我們的美國特色營運，包括 FreshPoint 新鮮蔬果配送業務、Buckhead | Newport Meat & Seafood 特色蛋白產品營運、以 Greco & Sons, Inc. 為核心的義大利特色產品平台、Edward Don 餐飲設備與供應品配送業務、亞洲特色配送公司以及若干不具重大影響力的其他小型特色業務；
•國際餐飲營運 – 包括美國以外的營運單位，提供完整的食品產品線以及廣泛的非食品產品。美洲地區主要包括加拿大、巴哈馬、哥斯達黎加與巴拿馬的營運單位，以及我們的出口營運單位，向國際客戶配送產品。我們的歐洲營運單位主要為英國 (U.K.)、法國、愛爾蘭與瑞典的營運單位；
•SYGMA – 我們的美國客製化配送營運，服務快速餐飲連鎖餐廳的營運點；
•其他 – 主要為我們的酒店供應營運，Guest Worldwide。
餐飲營運點提供完整的食品產品線以及廣泛的非食品產品至獨立與連鎖餐廳客戶、醫院、學校、酒店、工業餐飲服務及其他提供餐飲產品的場所。SYGMA 營運點提供完整的食品產品線以及廣泛的非食品產品至特定連鎖餐廳客戶營運點。有關各應報告分部的選取財務資料，以及地理區域的財務資訊，請參閱第 21 註釋 "業務分部資訊"，於第 8 項 "合併財務報表附註" 中。

paragraphs: 以下對 Sysco 會計年度截至 2026 年 6 月 27 日及 2025 年 6 月 28 日之財務狀況、營運成果及流動性與資本資源之討論與分析，應與我們之合併財務報表及附註說明，包含於本報告第 8 項項目中，並與本報告第二部分之 "Forward-looking Statements" 節及第一部分第 1A 項之 "Risk Factors" 節一併閱讀。本 Form 10-K 中已省略對 2025 財年與 3024 財年營運成果變動之討論，但可於 2025 年 6 月 28 日結業之 Form 10-K 中，第 7 項 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" 找到。該 Form 10-K 於 2025 年 8 月 22 日向證券交易委員會提交。
Sysco 將食品及相關產品分銷至餐廳、醫療與教育機構、住宿設施及其他食品服務客戶。我們主要營運地區為北美與歐洲。根據與企業分部揭露相關之會計規定，我們已將某些營運活動合併為三個應報告分部。"Other" 之財務資訊係屬未達定量揭露門檻之其他營運活動。
•美國餐飲服務業務 – 主要包括 (a) 我們的美國廣線業務，該業務分銷完整的食品產品，包括客製化切割肉類、海鮮、蔬果、義大利特色產品、特色進口品項以及廣泛的非食品產品，以及 (b) 我們的美國特色業務，包括我們的 FreshPoint 新鮮蔬果分銷業務，
我們的 Buckhead | Newport 肉類與海鮮特色蛋白業務，我們正在成長的義大利特色平台，以 Greco & Sons, Inc. 為核心，我們的 Edward Don 餐飲設備與供應品分銷業務，我們的亞洲特色分銷公司，以及若干不具重大影響力的其他特色業務。
•國際餐飲營運 – 包含美國境外的營運，提供完整線的食品產品以及廣泛的非食品產品。美洲地區主要包括加拿大、巴哈馬、哥斯大黎加和巴拿馬的營運，以及我們的出口營運，向國際客戶分銷產品。我們的歐洲營運主要包括英國（U.K.）、法國、愛爾蘭和瑞典的營運；
•SYGMA – 我們美國的客製化分銷營運，服務快速服務連鎖餐廳的營運點；和
•其他 – 主要為我們的飯店供應營運，Guest Worldwide。

我們估計，我們約服務美國約3770億美元年度餐飲市場的18%，根據Technomic, Inc.（Technomic）於2025年財務年度結束時取得的產業數據。Technomic預測市場規模將於2026年財務年度結束時增加至約3900億美元。有時Technomic可能會修訂用以計算餐飲市場規模的方法，因此我們的百分比不僅會因銷售結果而改變，也會因這樣的修訂而改變。我們也服務某些國際地區，這些地區的規模和市場佔有率各有不同。
根據產業來源，餐飲業，或稱為外食市場，代表美國消費者在消費層級所花費於食品購買總金額的約 56% ，截至 2025 年歷年終為止。

我們 2026 年財務年度的結果反映銷售成長 3.9% ，與 2025 年財務年度相比，主要由通貨膨脹與銷售量成長所驅動，包括近期收購的貢獻。銷售額在美國餐飲運營、國際餐飲運營與 SYGMA 分部均有所成長。毛利成長 4.5% ，與 2025 年財務年度相比，主要由於我們的戰略採購努力與來自本地客戶的銷售量增加。營運收入成長 0.2% ，與 2025 年財務年度相比，主要由於毛利增加，部分抵銷因增加銷售人力投資、增加重整與轉型專案成本、較高的績效報酬、以及較高的收購與盡職調查成本。我們將重整與轉型專案成本與收購與盡職調查成本視為 "Certain Item" 費用（如後文所定義）。扣除 Certain Item 費用後，調整後營運收入成長 2.6% ，與 2025 年財務年度相比。請見下方我們 2026 年財務年度結果與 2025 年財務年度結果的比較，兩者均包含與排除 Certain Items（如後文所定義）。
下方為 2026 年財務年度與 2025 年財務年度結果的比較：
•銷售額：◦成長 3.9% ，或 32 億美元，至 846 億美元；
•營運收入：◦成長 0.2%，或 7 百萬美元，至 3.1 十億美元；◦調整後營運收入成長 2.6%，或 91 百萬美元，至 3.6 十億美元；
•淨利潤：◦減少 3.9%，或 71 百萬美元，至 1.8 十億美元；◦調整後淨利潤成長 1.4%，或 31 百萬美元，至 2.2 十億美元；

headings: 風險因子總結
產業與總體經濟風險
業務與營運風險
與交易相關的風險
本公司所屬產業以低毛利率為特徵，且在出現顯著或持續性的通貨膨脹或通貨緊縮時，可能影響產品成本，並對本公司利潤及營運成果產生負面影響。
合格人力不足及勞動成本上升可能對本公司業務造成不利影響，並大幅降低營收。
全球衛生發展及因全球公共衛生危機所引發的經濟不確定性，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
不利的總體經濟環境，以及特定地方市場的不利條件，可能對本公司營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
總體經濟與政治不穩定以及法律法規的變更可能不利於我們的營運結果與財務狀況。
競爭以及政府採購組織（GPOs）的影響可能降低我們的毛利率，並使我們難以維持市場佔有率、成長速度與獲利能力。
關於我們的負面宣傳或對我們產品缺乏信心，可能對我們的聲譽造成負面影響，並降低營收。
我們與長期客戶的關係可能受到重大影響或終止，這可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果造成不利影響。
我們預期的客戶組成比例變動，即本地管理客戶與多單位客戶的比例，可能降低我們的毛利率與營運毛利。
消費者飲食習慣的變動可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。
拓展新市場與補充性業務線會帶來獨特的挑戰，且未必成功，若未能成功拓展，可能對我們業務策略的執行造成不利影響。
適用稅法或稅務規範的變更以及稅務爭議的解決，可能對我們的財務結果造成負面影響。
若本公司產品被指控導致傷害、疾病或死亡，或未符合政府規範，本公司可能需要召回或撤回產品，並可能面臨產品責任訴訟。
本公司可能因遵守環境法規而產生重大成本，並可能因未遵守而面臨重大罰款、處罰或第三方主張。
若本公司無法有效融資及整合取得之企業，每股盈餘可能受到重大不利影響。
本公司業務依賴技術，任何網路安全事件、其他技術中斷或實施新技術之延遲，可能對本公司業務及與客戶之關係造成負面影響。
paragraphs: 以下關於「風險因素」的討論識別出可能對我們業務、營運結果、財務狀況及未來財務表現產生不利影響的最重要因素。此資訊應與管理層對財務狀況及營運結果之討論與分析，以及本報告所包含之合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。以下關於風險的討論並非完整無遺，但係設計用以強調我們認為在評估我們業務時應考慮的最重要因素。這些因素可能導致我們未來的結果與我們在「管理層對財務狀況及營運結果之討論與分析」中所表達的預期，以及與其他歷史趨勢有所差異。
以下為可能對我們業務、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流產生重大且不利影響的主要風險摘要。此摘要並未說明我們所面對的所有風險，應與本項目 1A 以及本年度 10-K 報告其他地方所列的更詳細風險因素討論一併閱讀。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，也可能影響我們的業務。
• 我們所屬產業以低毛利率為特徵，且在出現顯著或持續的通貨膨脹或通貨緊縮期間，會影響我們產品的成本，並可能對我們的獲利能力及營運結果產生負面影響。
• 合格勞動力的短缺以及勞動成本的增加，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響，並導致營收大幅減少。
• 全球健康發展情況及因全球公共衛生危機所導致的經濟不確定性，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
• 不利的總體經濟條件，以及特定地方市場的不利條件，可能對我們的營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
